targets.text: microduck-cli sets up a MicroDuck environment (sim or real), trains and publishes policies through microduck_rl, drives the duck directly over robotd's JSON-RPC, and runs a data-only rules layer (events -> rules -> actions) — one CLI that any agent or human drives, implementing the upstream pollen-robotics docs and pointing users at them.

The announcement is true only if every operate verb works unchanged against BOTH 'robotd --fake' (CI) and 'robotd --sim' (MuJoCo) through the same socket client — no sim-specific code path above the transport seam.

No motor is ever commanded except as an intent through robotd's JSON-RPC (robot.move/head/look/do/init/relax/stop/setMode/loadPolicy). robotd is authoritative on safety (architecture.md §1.1 invariant 2: fall detection, joint/thermal limits, deadman, safe pose) and is the only process on the Dynamixel bus; microduck-cli never opens the serial port, never bypasses a clamp, and treats a refused intent as the correct answer.

A grep of microduck_cli/ finds no serial-port open, no Dynamixel/rustypot import and no write to /dev/tty*; every motion path ends in a JSON-RPC call, and a refused intent is reported by the daemon's reason code with exit 0 for the engine and exit 1 for a verb.

Transport is JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON over robotd's unix socket, implemented with stdlib socket+json only. The socket path is configurable (--socket / DUCK_SOCKET): in simulation it is the short state-dir path robotd --sim was started with (upstream's scripts/duck-sim uses $DUCK_SIM_STATE/duck-a.sock; a unix path is capped at ~108 bytes), and when a real duck exists the same client points at a forwarded /run/robotd.sock ('ssh -L …', cheatsheet-dev.md). Method names, API_VERSION, the 'hello' handshake, error codes and JOINT_NAMES come from duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs and are re-checked at connect. Continuous intents (robot.move/head/pose/mouth/sound hold) are sent as notifications at 20–50 Hz, last-writer-wins and expiring; discrete ones (robot.do/look/stop/enable/init/relax) as answered requests — the split the proto crate documents.

A daemon answering hello with a newer API_VERSION runs; an unknown method answers METHOD_NOT_FOUND and is logged as a named drop, never a traceback; a daemon whose JOINT_NAMES or obs/action lengths differ from the client's table refuses to start the engine with both numbers in the message.

Addressing follows upstream's simulation naming: a duck is a name (duck-a, duck-b …) that resolves to <state-dir>/<name>.sock (and <name>-tof.sock), the convention scripts/duck-sim establishes; DUCK_SIM_DUCK / --duck select one. duckctl (BLE, 'never on a robot') is wrapped only when a real duck exists — it is not a sim transport. The env doctor names exactly what is missing for the sim stack (a microduck clone on sim-remote-io, cargo/rust ≥1.89, a built robotd+robotctl, a microduck_rl .venv with libonnxruntime, a short state dir, a free body port) with the upstream doc line as the remediation.

Given a state dir and a name, the CLI resolves <state>/<name>.sock without any network or BLE call; env doctor on a box with no microduck clone, no cargo, no RL venv or no libonnxruntime lists each missing item with the upstream doc line and exits 2.

The operate surface uses robotctl's words so a command learned on the robot works here: robot init/relax/do/mode/look, policy list/load/add/remove/reset/search/check/update, pad status/bindings/bind/reset, health, monitor (--json NDJSON), configure --list, quack. It adds one verb robotctl lacks — a velocity 'move' driving robot.move with the deadman refreshed at intent rate, the way padd and the WebRTC console do — and every verb takes --json.

Every verb name and flag in the duck noun matches a robotctl subcommand of the same name (robot init/relax/do/mode/look, policy *, pad *, health, monitor, configure --list, quack) plus exactly one addition, move; a table test pins that list against robotctl's Namespace enum.

Every verb that moves or de-energizes the duck is gated the arm101 way: confirm on a TTY, print a zero-side-effect dry-run plan on a non-TTY without --apply, proceed on a non-TTY with --apply (agent mode). Applies to init, relax (which additionally keeps upstream's --yes semantics), do, move, mode, policy load/add/reset, and pad bind. Upstream's own safety wording is surfaced verbatim: 'init moves every joint — have the robot on its stand', 'relax cuts power and the robot collapses', 'stop zeroes intents and is NOT an emergency stop', 'nothing a stranger publishes is verified by anybody'.

Each gated verb has three tests: TTY without --apply prompts, non-TTY without --apply prints a plan and sends nothing (asserted on a --fake daemon's call log), non-TTY with --apply sends; the four upstream safety sentences appear verbatim in the verb's dry-run output.

The teach/train lane orchestrates microduck_rl by its documented commands, never by importing it: env check (CUDA GPU, uv, Python 3.12 (<3.13 pinned by bam), UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600 on ARM, hf auth, optional wandb), 'uv run list-envs', the mandatory 64-env/5-iter smoke test, 'uv run train <task> [--hf-jobs]', 'uv run play', 'uv run scripts/export.py' (the only safe ONNX path — normalizer baked in), 'uv run publish' (schema-2 manifest, [1,61]->[1,14] gate), then 'robotctl policy add|load' on the duck. The CLI plans and sequences that pipeline, records the artifacts (task id, run path, checkpoint, ONNX, HF repo), and points at AGENTS.md for reward design.

The train lane never imports mjlab_microduck; each stage is a subprocess whose argv equals the upstream-documented command, and the lane refuses to start a long run whose 64-env/5-iteration smoke test has not passed in this session or a recorded artifact.

microduck_rl is orchestrated as a sibling checkout via subprocess ('uv run --project <path> …'), never added as a dependency or extra of microduck-cli: its dependency tree (mjlab, warp, torch+CUDA, bam from git, requires-python <3.13) must not enter this package's resolution. Base runtime deps stay [] (CLAUDE.md hard constraint); if a hardware library is ever needed it goes behind an extra with a lazy import.
pyproject.toml dependencies stays []; a CI check fails if it is non-empty or if any [project.optional-dependencies] entry names mjlab, warp-lang, torch or better-actuator-models.

The rules layer follows reachy-mini-cli's shape: data-only TOML — [[react]] (when <predicate> then run <action>), [[inhibit]], [modes.<name>] — predicates as field/op/value over a sense snapshot (never code), unique ids, cooldown_s, hysteresis, bounded duration_s, two-layer per-id merge (shipped resource + box-local overlay with 'enabled = false' tombstones), fail-closed validation, and 'rules list/check/overview' verbs. Duck sense fields are derived from robot.state / robot.health / pad.input / tof.frame / chorale.heard (fallen, projected gravity, battery fraction, hottest servo, loop Hz, pad buttons, ToF nearest, nearby-duck beacons); actions are robotd intents (do <skill>, look, move, sound/quack, stop, mode).

RulesConfig.from_dict refuses every documented bad shape (unknown field, callable value, unknown skill, unknown predicate field/op, negative cooldown, duplicate id, unbounded looping) with the rule id in the message; a two-layer merge test proves per-id override and enabled=false tombstones survive an upgrade of the shipped layer.

Duck verbs land as noun groups in microduck_cli/cli/_commands/ following the cli.py pattern (parser_class=type(p), own 'overview', CliError-only failures, emit_result/emit_error split), with engine logic in sibling packages (microduck_cli/duck/, /rules/, /train/) and argparse wiring only in _commands/. Proposed nouns: 'env' (setup + doctor for sim/real/training), 'duck' (operate), 'policy' (train→export→publish→install pipeline), 'rules' (the neurosymbolic layer). Each new verb updates explain/catalog.py ENTRIES, overview.py _VERBS and learn.py in the same change, and 'teken cli doctor . --strict' stays green.

Every noun has an overview verb, every verb takes --json, and adding a verb without a catalog entry, an overview _VERBS line and a learn mention fails a lockstep test; teken cli doctor . --strict passes in CI.

The explain catalog and every error remediation point at the owning upstream page rather than restating it: docs/robot/cheatsheet.md (robotctl), docs/robot/duckctl.md, docs/policy-manifest.md, docs/design/architecture.md, microduck_rl AGENTS.md and scripts/hf/README.md. This honours upstream's own rule that one page owns a mechanism and everyone else says a sentence and points.

Each explain entry and each CliError remediation for a robot or training topic contains a URL into pollen-robotics/microduck or microduck_rl docs, and a test asserts no explain body restates a robotctl command table longer than three lines.

The env noun brings up and checks the simulation stack by reproducing upstream's documented steps (or shelling out to scripts/duck-sim when the clone has it): clone/checkout microduck at sim-remote-io, 'cargo build -p robotd -p robotctl -p tof -p sounds', locate libonnxruntime in the microduck_rl .venv, generate a params toml naming the policy files from the clone, start 'duck-body' on a port then 'robotd --sim host:port --socket <state>/<name>.sock', wait for 'hello' + robot.health, and optionally 'robot.init'. It supports N ducks (one port each, one MuJoCo world), a scene (bare floor or apartment), headless mode, and a --fake backend for tests; 'env down' stops by pidfile after confirming /proc cmdline (upstream's stop_one lesson), never by name.

env up on a box with the two clones and a synced RL venv reaches robot.health healthy within 60 s on --fake and within 120 s on --sim; env down leaves no robotd, duck-body or tofd process and never signals a pid whose /proc cmdline does not match.

The engine package (microduck_cli/behavior/ or engine/) mirrors reachy-mini-cli's shape so it can be extracted: engine.run(tick_seam=…) with a TickBus of drivers; a pure data model (channels, StopClass priorities, Lifetime) with duck channels = the intent families robotd exposes (twist, head, body pose, mouth, sound, skill); SenseProviders fed from robot.subscribe/robot.state + robot.health polled at 2 Hz + tof.frame + chorale.heard (peek callables, *_age_s freshness, None on failure); a TargetSink that emits intents through the JSON-RPC client; rules-as-data loaded in two layers; bounded lifetimes fail-closed; senselog drop reasons on stderr; a state.json heartbeat so a second engine process refuses early. No SDK, transport or CLI error type is imported below the composition root.

The engine adds no command filtering of its own: robotd's cmd_alpha/head_alpha EMA (0.2 default in deploy/robotd.toml) is treated as part of the plant, so a rule's step command arrives as the ramp the daemon documents.

Instruction injection has ONE admission path: a KindRegistry-style registry that validates fail-closed and admits (a) intents fired by react rules and (b) ad-hoc intents an agent or human sends via a CLI verb (e.g. 'duck intent <kind> …' / a spool file) — same validator, same bounds (duration caps, per-axis limits, cooldowns), same named refusals. Rules are the durable form of an instruction; an ad-hoc intent is the one-shot form. Every admitted instruction becomes robotd intents that robotd's own safety may still refuse, and the refusal is surfaced by name.

One KindRegistry instance serves both rule-fired and CLI-injected intents: a test injects the same over-limit payload by both paths and gets the same refusal text; a static check finds no second validator.

The train lane targets three local hosts (DGX Spark GB10, Jetson Thor, Jetson AGX Orin) plus Hugging Face Jobs, and its env doctor detects which it is on (uname -m, nvidia-smi / JetPack markers, CUDA version) and reports whether microduck_rl's pinned torch source applies. wandb is optional: the lane runs without a key and only passes --wandb-run-path / forwards a key when configured.

env doctor on GB10, Jetson Thor and AGX Orin prints the detected host class and whether microduck_rl's torch source applies; with no wandb key the smoke test still runs and play/export accept a local checkpoint path.

This repo's CLAUDE.md and README are updated in the first engine PR to record decision c20: the engine lives here for now, is built extraction-first, and neurosymbolic-system is the later home — replacing the current 'a tick loop here belongs upstream' guidance so a reviewer does not reject the engine on stale instructions.
The first engine PR's diff touches CLAUDE.md's neurosymbolic-system section and cicd/SKILL.md's triage defaults, replacing the 'engine belongs upstream' guidance with the extraction-first decision.

Two kinds of operator, one surface: (1) AI agents on the AgentCulture mesh (any backend — the colleague resident, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot) that set up the duck's environment, author rules, inject ad-hoc instructions, and run training without a human at the keyboard; (2) the human who owns the duck and does the same things interactively. Every verb serves both: --json and --apply for agents, TTY confirmation and readable text for the human.
Every duck verb runs unattended with --json --apply in a non-TTY test and interactively with a prompt in a pty test; no verb requires a TTY to succeed.

A person or agent runs one CLI to (a) bring up a MicroDuck — today the MuJoCo twin driven by the real robotd, later a physical duck at the same socket contract — and know from 'env doctor' exactly what is missing; (b) operate it in robotctl's own words plus velocity 'move', with motion gated; (c) train, export, publish and install a policy through microduck_rl's documented pipeline on a local GPU box or HF Jobs; and (d) run an off-board engine whose data-only rules turn observed events into injected instructions, with agents able to inject ad-hoc instructions through the same admission path. The duck keeps whatever autonomy upstream ships; this layer sits above it.
The six success-signal commands of c30 all pass on the dev box against --sim, and the operate verbs pass unchanged against --fake in CI.

Today driving a MicroDuck means reading two upstream repos, hand-assembling a sim from a branch, a params file, a dlopen'd ONNX runtime and a socket path, and typing raw robotctl or gamepad input; teaching it means a separate GPU project with its own conventions. None of that is agent-operable and all of it is re-derived per person. One CLI that implements those docs — and links to them — lets any agent or human spare that work, and gives the engine that neurosymbolic-system will be extracted from a second robot to generalise against.
A clean-box walkthrough of env doctor → env up → duck health needs no manual params file, ORT path or socket path from the operator; each is derived or reported.

Observable when done: 'microduck env up --sim' on a clean box (given the two upstream clones) yields a standing duck and 'microduck duck health --json' reports healthy at 50 Hz; 'microduck duck do roulade --apply' runs a skill in sim; a rules.toml with one react rule fires an intent visible in 'duck monitor' within its cooldown and 'rules check' refuses a malformed one; the train lane's smoke test (64 envs, 5 iters) runs end to end locally and the same command submits to HF Jobs; 'teken cli doctor . --strict', the lint stack and coverage ≥60% stay green with zero base dependencies.
Each of the six checks is a named CI job or a documented manual step with its expected output recorded in docs/, and a failing check blocks the PR that regresses it.

The engine yields to a human driver. robotd applies intents last-writer-wins with no arbitration between clients, and padd (gamepad), the mediad console and a second CLI all send the same robot.move/head/pose notifications. The engine therefore watches pad.input (padd's raw tap) and robot.remoteSessionActive, and while a human is driving it inhibits its own continuous intents (a named 'human-driving' drop) — rules that fire a discrete skill are still admitted but robotd's refusal, if any, is surfaced by name.

With a --fake daemon and a simulated pad.input stream, the engine's call log shows zero robot.move/head/look/pose/do/setMode calls while the pad is active and a human-driving drop count on stderr; sound and mouth calls continue.

'robot.enable' is part of the gated-motion set alongside init/relax/do/move/mode (it 'can bring a limp robot up as a side effect of being asked to drive'), and the engine's start sequence is explicit: connect → hello (API version) → health → init (gated) → enable (gated) → rules armed. A skill fired by a rule while the robot is not driving is refused by robotd ('press Start first'); the engine surfaces that as a named drop rather than retrying.
A rule that fires a skill before enable produces a named drop and no retry; init and enable each pass the three gate tests of c7; the engine's start log shows the six steps in order.

'rules check' validates every action a rule names against what THIS duck actually has: the skill list comes from robot.policies at check time (or from a recorded skills snapshot for offline checks), a rule naming a missing skill is reported by id with the robot's list — the same behaviour upstream gives a pad binding for a skill the robot does not have. Skill names are never assumed from a static table.
rules check against a --fake daemon reporting skills [a, b] refuses a rule naming c with 'c not in [a, b]' and the rule id; --replay with a recorded skills snapshot gives the same answer offline.

microduck-cli never writes /etc/robot/robotd.toml or the params file of a running daemon: policy slots change only through robot.loadPolicy / robotctl policy (robotd writes the key under a file lock), pad bindings only through pad.bind, config only through robotctl configure. The CLI surfaces upstream's durability verbatim — a policy load 'survives a reboot and survives updates'; 'policy reset' puts it back — so a trial never silently becomes the boot default without saying so.

A grep of microduck_cli/ finds no open of robotd.toml or updater.toml for writing; the only file the env noun writes is the sim params file, before robotd is started; policy load's text output contains 'survives a reboot' and names policy reset.

Own what you energize: on any abnormal engine exit (exception, Ctrl-C, socket error) the engine best-effort sends robot.stop, robot.pose {active:false}, robot.mouth 0 and robot.sound hold:false, each independently so one failure does not skip the rest, then exits non-zero naming what it could not send. It does NOT relax the robot (a deliberate hold must survive; relax collapses it). A dead socket is stated as the limit: robotd's own deadman zeroes velocity, but a held pose/mouth outlives us until its notification expires.

Killing the engine with SIGINT mid-behaviour against a --fake daemon yields exactly stop, pose active:false, mouth 0 and sound hold:false in its call log, no relax, and a non-zero exit naming any release that failed when one is forced to fail.

The JSON-RPC client is a background I/O thread pair (writer with a bounded outbound queue; reader correlating replies by id and fanning notifications such as robot.state to peek slots). The tick thread only does put_nowait: a full queue, a wedged socket or a slow daemon resolve to a named drop ('ipc-queue-full', 'ipc-down'), never to a blocked tick. Requests from verbs (do/look/init) wait on their own future with a timeout; notifications are fire-and-forget.
A test that wedges the fake socket shows the tick period unchanged (measured over 100 ticks) and an ipc-down drop; a test that fills the queue shows an ipc-queue-full drop and no blocked tick.

The shipped default rules are few and safety-first, mirroring default_rules.toml's discipline: an inhibit rule that disables every skill and the idle base while robot.state reports fallen (recovery is the daemon's/VelStand policy's job), a low-battery inhibit keyed on robot.health's charge fraction, and at most one or two reactions that are obviously correct in any room. Rule ids are a public interface pinned by a test; everything else is the operator's overlay.
The shipped rules file contains at most four rules; a test pins their ids; a replay of a recorded fall shows every skill and the idle base inhibited within one tick of fallen=true.

No secret ever reaches stdout or a --json payload: HF_TOKEN, wandb keys, DUCK_PIN and the sim's account token file are reported as set/unset by 'env doctor' and never echoed; the train lane passes them by environment to subprocesses, never on a command line (visible in /proc cmdline).

A test sets HF_TOKEN, DUCK_PIN and a wandb key to sentinel strings and asserts none appears in any stdout, --json or stderr output of env doctor, train or duck verbs, nor in any subprocess argv the lane spawns.

'duck record' captures robot.state (via robot.subscribe), robot.health polls, pad.input and tof.frame to JSONL with monotonic timestamps — the artifact 'rules check --replay' and the engine's offline tests consume, and the source of truth for the duck sense-field vocabulary (resolving the parked unknown about the state payload). Stdout stays pure JSONL; all diagnostics go to stderr.
duck record against --fake writes one JSON object per line with a monotonic timestamp and source tag; stdout contains nothing but JSONL; rules check --replay accepts that file.

rules.toml carries a schema_version; the loader refuses an unknown or missing version fail-closed with the fix named. This is what lets the schema move to neurosymbolic-system later without silently reinterpreting an operator's overlay.
A rules.toml without schema_version or with an unknown one is refused with the expected version named; the shipped layer and every fixture carry the current version.

tasks.summary: IPC protocol table — microduck_cli/ipc/proto.py: method names, API_VERSION, JOINT_NAMES (15), POLICY_OBS_LEN 61 / ACTION_LEN 14, JSON-RPC + duck error codes, and a continuous-vs-discrete classification (notification vs request) per method, transcribed from duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs at a pinned commit
acceptance_criteria: A table test asserts every constant against a fixture copied from the pinned duck-ipc-proto commit and fails if the fixture and the table disagree
is_notification(method) returns True for robot.move/head/pose/mouth/sound-hold and False for robot.do/look/stop/enable/init/relax/setMode/loadPolicy
The module imports nothing outside the stdlib
tasks.instruction: Own only microduck_cli/ipc/proto.py and its tests; transcribe from the pinned duck-ipc-proto commit recorded in docs/, never from memory; keep the module stdlib-only.

tasks.summary: In-process fake robotd for tests — tests/fake_robotd.py: a unix-socket JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON server speaking the proto table (hello, robot.health, robot.subscribe/state stream at a configurable rate, robot.policies/skills, init/enable/relax/do/look/stop/move/pose/mouth/sound, pad.input tap, tof.frame) that records every call in order, can be told to refuse a method with a reason, answer METHOD_NOT_FOUND, report fallen, wedge, or delay replies
acceptance_criteria: A test opens the fake, sends hello and gets API_VERSION back; an unknown method returns JSON-RPC -32601 with the method name
Call log preserves order and distinguishes notifications (no id) from requests (id) so later tests can assert exact sequences
wedge() makes the server stop reading; delay(ms) delays replies; both are used by the client tests
Safe under pytest -n auto: each instance binds its own short temp socket path (< 100 bytes)
tasks.instruction: Own tests/fake_robotd.py and tests/test_fake_robotd.py only. Model the wire on duck-ipc-proto: JSON-RPC 2.0, one object per line, notifications have no id. Bind each instance to a short path under tempfile.mkdtemp (assert < 100 bytes). Expose: call_log (ordered, with a 'kind' of request|notification), refuse(method, code, message), wedge(), delay(ms), set_state(fallen=..., skills=[...]), and a state stream at a configurable Hz. No third-party imports.

tasks.summary: Rules data model — microduck_cli/behavior/rules.py + tests/test_rules.py: schema_version, [[react]] / [[inhibit]] / [modes], Predicate as field/op/value, RulesConfig.from_dict as the single fail-closed gate, per-id two-layer merge with enabled=false tombstones, cooldown_s / hysteresis / bounded duration_s, duck SENSE_FIELDS and ACTION vocabulary placeholders
acceptance_criteria: from_dict refuses unknown field, callable value, unknown predicate field or op, negative cooldown, duplicate id, unbounded looping action, and names the rule id in every message
merge_rules: overlay entry with a matching id replaces wholesale keeping position; a new id appends; enabled=false disables the shipped id
A file without schema_version or with an unknown one is refused naming the expected version
Module imports nothing from the CLI, the IPC client, or any transport
tasks.instruction: Own microduck_cli/behavior/rules.py and tests/test_rules.py. Mirror reachy-mini-cli reachy/behavior/rules.py's from_dict gate and merge_rules semantics (read it, do not copy prose). Add schema_version = 1 as a required top-level int; refuse absent or unknown with the expected version in the message. Sense field and action name sets are frozen sets imported from behavior/sense.py once t4 lands — until then define them locally and mark with a TODO(t4) that t11 removes.

tasks.summary: Behavior model and sense snapshot — microduck_cli/behavior/model.py + sense.py + tests: duck channels (twist, head, pose, mouth, sound, skill), StopClass priorities, Lifetime, Behavior spec + contribution fn; Sense snapshot (fallen, gravity, battery_frac, hottest_servo_c, loop_hz, pad_active, remote_session, tof_nearest_m, skills, *_age_s) and SenseProviders as injected zero-arg peek callables degrading to None
acceptance_criteria: A provider that raises, returns None, or is missing yields the same None field and never propagates
Arbitration test: a higher StopClass owns a contested channel; PASSIVE only fills an unclaimed one; UNSTOPPABLE/STOPPING block admission
Every sense field a rule predicate can name is declared once in a frozen set the rules module imports
tasks.instruction: Own microduck_cli/behavior/model.py, sense.py and their tests. Channels are the duck's intent families: twist, head, pose, mouth, sound, skill. Sense fields are provisional (risk on this task): fallen, gravity (3), battery_frac, hottest_servo_c, loop_hz, pad_active, remote_session, tof_nearest_m, skills, plus *_age_s for each — expect a rename pass after t18's first real recording. No I/O, no transport, no CLI imports.

tasks.summary: Motion gate helper — microduck_cli/duck/gate.py + tests: the arm101 tri-state (TTY prompt / non-TTY dry-run plan with zero sends / non-TTY --apply proceeds), plus the four upstream safety sentences as constants rendered verbatim into every dry-run plan
acceptance_criteria: consent(args, plan) returns PROMPT on a TTY without --apply, DRY_RUN on a non-TTY without --apply, APPLY with --apply; a pty test and a non-TTY test cover all three
Dry-run output contains the exact strings for init (moves every joint, on its stand), relax (collapses), stop (not an emergency stop) and community policies (verified by nobody)
tasks.instruction: Own microduck_cli/duck/gate.py and tests/test_gate.py. Copy the tri-state semantics from arm101-cli calibrate.py / set_baudrate.py (read, do not paste): TTY without --apply prompts; non-TTY without --apply prints a plan and performs zero sends; non-TTY with --apply proceeds. The four safety sentences are module constants quoted verbatim from microduck docs/robot/cheatsheet.md and duckctl.md. Use a pty in tests for the TTY branch.

tasks.summary: Duck addressing — microduck_cli/duck/addressing.py + tests: name -> <state>/<name>.sock and <name>-tof.sock, DUCK_SIM_STATE / DUCK_SIM_DUCK / --duck / --socket precedence, the 108-byte socket path check, and a 'no such duck' CliError that lists the sockets present in the state dir
acceptance_criteria: resolve('duck-b') returns the expected paths with no network or subprocess call (asserted by monkeypatching socket and subprocess)
A resolved path longer than 100 bytes raises CliError exit 2 naming the limit and DUCK_SIM_STATE
tasks.instruction: Own microduck_cli/duck/addressing.py and tests/test_addressing.py. Precedence: --socket > --duck/DUCK_SIM_DUCK + DUCK_SIM_STATE (default ~/.cache/duck-sim) > first *.sock in the state dir. Return both <name>.sock and <name>-tof.sock. Raise CliError exit 2 with the sockets present when the name is unknown, and when a path exceeds 100 bytes.

tasks.summary: Static guard tests and CI wiring — tests/test_zero_deps.py (dependencies == [] and no extra names mjlab/warp-lang/torch/better-actuator-models), tests/test_no_hardware_paths.py (no serial/rustypot/dynamixel import, no /dev/tty open under microduck_cli/), tests/test_no_config_writes.py (no write-open of robotd.toml/updater.toml), tests/test_no_secrets_in_output.py scaffold (sentinel env values never appear in captured stdout/stderr/argv), and .markdownlint-cli2.yaml ignoring docs/specs/** and docs/plans/**
acceptance_criteria: Each guard test fails when a fixture module violating it is added under microduck_cli/ (asserted by writing a temp module inside the test)
markdownlint-cli2 passes on the exported spec in docs/specs/ with the new ignore
The secrets test exposes a helper assert_no_secrets(captured, argv_log) that later noun tests reuse
tasks.instruction: Own the four guard tests, .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, and only the lines of .github/workflows/tests.yml you add. Each guard writes a temporary violating module under a tmp copy of microduck_cli/ to prove it fails. test_no_secrets_in_output exports assert_no_secrets(captured_text, argv_list) reused by t14/t15/t18/t19. Add docs/specs/** and docs/plans/** to markdownlint ignores; run markdownlint on both exported files.

tasks.summary: Host detection for the train lane — microduck_cli/env/hosts.py + tests: classify GB10 (DGX Spark), Jetson Thor, Jetson AGX Orin, other aarch64, x86_64 and 'hf-jobs' from uname/nvidia-smi/JetPack markers (all injected for tests), and report whether microduck_rl's torch source (cu129 index, linux-aarch64) applies
